article.title: What we store, and for how long
article.excerpt: The platform keeps metadata about your messages, not their content. Here is exactly what that means for your own records.

p: The platform does not persist the text of your messages. It is not needed to deliver them, and keeping it would mean holding customer content that carries no operational value here.
The practical consequence: if you need a record of what you sent, keep your own copy. It cannot be reconstructed from the log.

head: Stored
Why
rows: So the log can answer what happened to a message
Provider message ID and raw status
For reconciliation with your provider account
For audit, and so a STOP is not lost
So the platform can send through your provider account

p: Log retention follows the plan, and records past the window are removed automatically rather than by request.
sections.scope: Suppression records are not subject to the log retention window — a consent record must outlive a message log to be worth anything.

p: The log can be exported, and the same metadata is available over the API. Exports are asynchronous and truncate at 1,000,000 rows, and a truncated export says so rather than quietly shortening the file.
